name: Autosomal Dominant Limb-Girdle Muscular Dystrophy Type 1B

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic Criteria for Limb-Girdle Muscular Dystrophy

criteria.description: Progressive proximal muscle weakness predominantly affecting shoulder and pelvic girdles
Autosomal dominant inheritance pattern with affected first-degree relatives
Identification of pathogenic mutations in the LMNA gene
Muscle biopsy showing dystrophic changes with variable fibrosis and fiber size variation

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of progressive proximal muscle weakness with autosomal dominant family history plus identification of LMNA gene mutation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic confirmation is essential for definitive diagnosis; muscle biopsy and EMG are supportive.

searchTerms: gradual weakness of shoulder and hip muscles

pathognomonic.symptomName: Cardiac conduction defects including atrioventricular block
searchTerms: heart rhythm problems with AV block

pathognomonic.symptomName: Muscle atrophy predominantly in shoulder and pelvic girdle muscles
searchTerms: muscle wasting in shoulder and hip areas
loss of muscle bulk near trunk
mild weakness in hands and feet

occasional.symptomName: Respiratory muscle weakness leading to dyspnea on exertion
searchTerms: weak breathing muscles causing shortness of breath

occasional.symptomName: Dysphagia due to pharyngeal muscle involvement
searchTerms: difficulty swallowing from throat muscle weakness
swallowing problems due to muscle involvement

occasional.symptomName: Mild neuropathic symptoms such as paresthesias
searchTerms: slight numbness or pins and needles

rare.symptomName: Severe heart failure secondary to dilated cardiomyopathy
searchTerms: severe heart failure from enlarged heart

laboratory: Elevated serum creatine kinase (mild to moderate elevation)
imaging: Muscle MRI showing fatty replacement and atrophy of proximal muscles
Echocardiogram revealing conduction abnormalities or cardiomyopathy
genetic: Pathogenic mutations in LMNA gene confirming diagnosis
other: Electromyography showing myopathic motor unit potentials
Muscle biopsy with dystrophic features and fibrosis

distinguishingFeatures: Facial and scapular muscle involvement predominant

redFlags: Rapid progression of muscle weakness over weeks
New onset cardiac conduction block or arrhythmia
references: Mercuri E, Muntoni F. Muscular Dystrophies. Lancet. 2013;381(9869):845-860.
